overview: Leprosy is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae, affecting the skin, peripheral nerves, mucosa of the upper respiratory tract, and eyes. It can cause progressive and permanent disabilities if left untreated. However, leprosy is curable with multidrug therapy (MDT) and early treatment can prevent disability.
symptoms: Loss of sensation in skin patches
Weakness of muscles supplied by affected nerves
Definite loss of sensation in skin patches
transmission: Droplets from the nose and mouth of an untreated case
Prolonged, close contact with an untreated case
key_facts: Leprosy is curable with multidrug therapy (MDT)
Elimination of leprosy as a public health problem was achieved globally in 2000
117 countries reported fewer than 1000 new cases in 2024
